---
title: "Zeros in count data"
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

More observed zeros than a Poisson model predicts do not by themselves establish a separate zero-generating process. We examine that **zero-pattern ambiguity** in Storme's ([2024](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11525-024-09429-8)) French liaison study and its [Zenodo release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12733801). One prepared row is a final-morpheme, final-consonant, and liaison-status combination. Following the released code, the response is integer truncation of 100 times summed `freqfilms2`, not a direct token tally. The Zenodo record states no separate data license, so these notes do not redistribute it.

```{r}
#| label: load-storme-zero
#| echo: true
path <- "data/storme-liaison/storme-liaison-counts.csv"
if (file.exists(path)) {
  storme <- read.csv(path)
} else {
  url <- paste0("https://zenodo.org/api/records/12733801/files/",
                "study1-data.csv/content")
  source_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  download.file(url, source_file, mode = "wb")
  stopifnot(unname(tools::md5sum(source_file)) ==
              "8a7788489b6820822cda3f338881f77e")
  raw <- read.csv(source_file, check.names = FALSE)
  storme <- aggregate(freqfilms2 ~ final_morph + FinalConsonant + Liaison,
                      raw, sum)
  storme$reconstructed_count <- as.integer(storme$freqfilms2 * 100)
  names(storme)[1:4] <- c("final_morpheme", "final_consonant", "liaison",
                          "frequency_per_million_sum")
}
stopifnot(nrow(storme) == 11195L)
storme$liaison <- factor(storme$liaison, levels = c("no", "yes"))
storme$final_consonant <- factor(storme$final_consonant)
```

We fit additive Poisson and negative-binomial baselines with the same mean formula. The negative binomial allows

$$
\operatorname{Var}[Y_i\mid\mu_i]=\mu_i+\frac{\mu_i^2}{\theta},
$$

so ordinary heterogeneity can increase both tails, including zero mass.

```{r}
#| label: compare-zero-probabilities
#| echo: true
poisson_fit <- glm(reconstructed_count ~ liaison + final_consonant,
                   poisson(), storme)
nb_fit <- MASS::glm.nb(reconstructed_count ~ liaison + final_consonant,
                       data = storme, control = glm.control(maxit = 100L))
storme$observed_zero <- storme$reconstructed_count == 0L
storme$poisson_zero <- dpois(0L, fitted(poisson_fit))
storme$nb_zero <- dnbinom(0L, size = nb_fit$theta, mu = fitted(nb_fit))
zeros <- aggregate(cbind(observed_zero, poisson_zero, nb_zero) ~ liaison,
                   storme, mean)
zeros
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-zero-comparison
#| echo: true
library(ggplot2)
zero_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(liaison = zeros$liaison, model = "Observed", value = zeros$observed_zero),
  data.frame(liaison = zeros$liaison, model = "Poisson", value = zeros$poisson_zero),
  data.frame(liaison = zeros$liaison, model = "Negative binomial", value = zeros$nb_zero)
)
zero_long$model <- factor(zero_long$model,
                          levels = c("Observed", "Poisson", "Negative binomial"))
ggplot(zero_long, aes(model, value, shape = liaison)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = .35), size = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Probability of a zero", shape = NULL) +
  theme_classic()
```

The Poisson model assigns almost no zero mass, while the negative binomial moves toward the observed proportions without a structural-zero component. We thus do not fit a zero-inflated model here. Such a model requires a linguistically motivated process that makes some morpheme cells deterministically absent, not merely a conspicuous zero bar.
